HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P) NOTE

Patient: Joe Bloggs DOB 07 Jun 1974 (Reports age 53–54)  
Visit type: Video consultation

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden‐onset mid-sternal chest pressure (“like someone sitting on my chest”) that began while gardening ≈2 hours prior to call.  
• Severity & course: Constant, 7/10 intensity, unchanged since onset.  
• Radiation: To left shoulder and arm; no radiation to head, right arm, or back.  
• Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, light-headedness, persistent nausea (no vomiting), recent exertional dyspnoea on stairs/uphill, calf pain, and leg swelling.  
• Aggravating/alleviating factors: Began with mild exertion; no specific relief measures attempted; persists at rest.  
• Previous episodes: None reported.  
• Social: Current smoker (amount not stated); lives with wife.  
• No reported dysphagia, bowel/bladder changes, or recent trauma.

Past Medical History:
• Hypertension (untreated)  
• Hypercholesterolaemia (untreated)  
• No other chronic illnesses disclosed.  
Allergies: Not documented.  
Medications: None reported (no antihypertensives or lipid-lowering agents).

Physical Examination:
• Remote consultation; no objective vitals or examination performed.  
• Patient reported: chest pressure present, dyspnoea present, alert and oriented, able to speak in full sentences.  
• No throat swelling, no difficulty swallowing, no vomiting.

Impression:
Suspected acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina/NSTEMI) based on sudden persistent pressure-type chest pain with left-arm radiation and autonomic symptoms in a patient with multiple cardiovascular risk factors.  
Top DDx considerations consistent with presentation:  
1. Acute coronary syndrome – most likely.  
2. Pulmonary embolism – consider given dyspnoea, calf pain, leg swelling.  
3. Aortic dissection – lower likelihood but hypertension increases risk; pain character less typical.

Management Plan:
• Emergency services (ambulance) activated during call for immediate transfer to hospital for cardiac evaluation.  
• Advised patient to remain calm, seated, and hydrate with small sips of water; avoid taking any medications until assessed by paramedics.  
• Instructed patient to inform wife and prepare essentials for hospital.  
• Anticipated ED work-up: ECG, cardiac biomarkers, chest imaging, full vitals, oxygen administration, IV access.  
• Follow-up: Physician will review hospital findings once available and schedule follow-up appointment post-discharge.

Patient Summary:
Middle-aged male with untreated hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, and smoking history developed acute mid-sternal pressure radiating to left arm with dyspnoea and nausea. Clinical picture concerning for acute coronary syndrome; ambulance arranged for urgent hospital assessment.

Key Takeaways:
• Chest pressure with arm radiation and breathlessness can indicate a heart attack—seek emergency care immediately.  
• Stay seated and calm while awaiting paramedics; do not self-medicate.  
• Wife to accompany and bring necessary personal items for hospital stay.

Next Steps:
• Hospital ED: ECG, troponins, chest X-ray/CT as indicated, anticoagulation or reperfusion therapy per protocol.  
• Outpatient: Initiate guideline-directed medical therapy for HTN and hyperlipidaemia after acute event; smoking cessation support.
